setup: Start with the bench at a slight decline
Hook your feet under the pads
Lie back, hands lightly by your head
execution: Breathe out and curl your ribs toward your hips
Lift your shoulders and upper back only
Keep your lower back on the pad
faults: Don't sit all the way up from the hips

notes: Start with a shallow angle; each step steeper makes it harder.
Get on and off carefully: sit up fully before you unhook your feet.
Lying head-down makes some people light-headed. Sit up slowly between sets and stop if you feel dizzy.
To add load, hold a plate on your chest and log it as added weight.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at bench height. Decline bench angled with the head end low on the left and the foot rollers high on the right. Keep the angle shallow (about 20-30°).

keyPositions.label: Down
keyPositions.describe: Lying back on the decline bench, head lower than hips, knees bent with feet hooked under the rollers. Back flat on the pad, hands lightly by the head.

keyPositions.label: Curled
keyPositions.describe: Head, shoulders and upper back curled up off the pad, ribs drawn toward the hips. Lower back and hips still on the pad; the hips don't bend further.

ikHints: Hips and lower back fixed on the pad
emphasise: Only the upper back lifts off the pad
Hips don't bend; this is a curl, not a sit-up
